---
description: 'Use when adding, correcting, renaming or removing winery French and English locale messages.'
applyTo: 'i18n/locales/*.json'
---

# Internationalization Instructions

Use [i18n](../../.agents/skills/i18n/SKILL.md) for key parity, syntax, reactive consumers and route continuity.
Use [content direction](../../.agents/docs/content-direction.md) for estate voice, wine facts and natural English.

Keep French as source and English equivalent in factual meaning and visitor access.
The locale files are [fr-FR.json](../../i18n/locales/fr-FR.json) and [en-US.json](../../i18n/locales/en-US.json).
Use US English and the [content naming map](../../.agents/skills/i18n/references/content-naming.md) for namespaces and stable IDs.
New multiword keys use snake_case; keep stable media/project/wine IDs independent of spelling conventions for ordinary message fields.
Add, rename and remove key identities in both locales together, preserving value shapes and interpolation names.
Update literal and generated consumers when a key changes.
A wording correction in one language does not require an unrelated edit to correct copy elsewhere.

Preserve official wine/appellation names, vintages and supplied quantities.
Keep image alternatives, accessible labels, form feedback, errors and metadata translated.
Do not derive business facts from filenames or fill missing information with invented text.
Keep proper names and factual data in their shared owner where appropriate.
Use `components.*` for component-owned controls and `pages.*` for page prose; keep `tab_name`, `pictures.*` and `seo.*` distinct.

Preserve two-space JSON indentation and existing useful ordering.
Check Vue I18n syntax for `|`, `@` and braces; JSON parsing alone is insufficient.
Do not introduce arbitrary HTML rendering for translated prose.
Check affected leaf-key and placeholder parity and compile changed messages through available project checks.
Inspect affected consumers after a locale switch without a reload or viewport resize.
